title: Video lab: title editor, cinema sound, wide gamut, timeline skin, WebGPU player
blurb: Five experiments with a video as a canvas child. Clips and editable HTML title cards joined by shader transitions and exported to a file, a cinema screen in a 3D room with the sound placed at the screen, a wide-gamut clip in a Display P3 canvas, a shader on the native timeline only, and the player shader in WGSL.
question: Can clips and HTML title cards be cut together and exported from one canvas, does a video keep its native controls and wide-gamut colours on a quad in perspective and in a Display P3 canvas, and does the player shader run in WebGPU?
result: Yes for the editor, the export, the controls in perspective, the sound position, the timeline skin and Display P3. An HDR10 clip is tone-mapped to at most 1.0. The WGSL shader was rendered off screen only: the test browser cannot show a WebGPU canvas.
